evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52h = 10.49 mg/L, well above the 2 mg/L limit; minimum observed DO2 = 7.77 mg/L at 27.8h
Receiving P assays: 0.047 g/L (12h), 0.014 (24h), 1.017 (36h), 2.984 g/L (48h) — matches source batches' normal production curve (source P at 48h: 3.06, 3.02, 2.98)
Receiving DO2 profile including ~24h dip, 28h jump, and 75h-style recovery mirrors source-1/2/3 trajectories
Forward model KEEP: 576 kg product, min DO 7.20 mg/L, zero oxygen deficit, all 5 sensitivity members feasible
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation is tracking the healthy source-batch trajectories closely: DO2 profile (dip to ~7.8–8.4 mg/L at 24–28h, recovery jumps at 28h) matches all three source batches, and delayed P assays (36h: 1.02 g/L, 48h: 2.98 g/L) match source values (1.02–1.12, 2.98–3.06 g/L). DO2 at 52h is ~10.5 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L minimum with no oxygen deficit. The forward model under KEEP predicts ~576 kg product mass, min DO ~7.2 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, and feasibility across all sensitivity members. Interventions (feed reduction) would lower growth/product formation without any oxygen-constraint benefit; stop would forfeit all production. This is a normal case requiring no intervention.
args.uncertainty: Forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not the hidden receiving realization; DO2 is noisy online sensor data with a systematic step at 28h/75h. However, deviation from source baselines is small and consistent across both DO2 and P assays, so KEEP risk is low. If hidden receiving parameters are worse than nominal, min DO margin (7.2 vs 2.0 mg/L limit) is still wide.
